tasks.task: Pick the right chart for a message and write its spec

items.when: When there is a small table and a point to make and the chart type is not chosen
When the chart must be written in full as Vega-Lite, Chart.js or spreadsheet steps
When the client should see a drawn alternative, as an image or an interactive plot
When a chart is correct but unclear, to separate what it shows from what readers assume
When the spec is drafted, to check the type, axes and colours do not mislead

tasks.task: Make a set of charts for one message

items.when: When a request for charts arrives and you need the steps from brief to published
Before any chart, to fix the point, the proof and the next step for the reader
When each chart needs its own message, headline and full spec
When you want several versions drawn in code to compare before choosing
When every chart shows everything, to bring out the one thing the reader must see
Before the set goes into a report, deck or post

tasks.task: Review existing charts and list the fixes

items.when: When charts or results slides may mislead, exclude or confuse readers
When one chart is questioned and needs a quick, clear verdict
When a chart looks impressive, to check its scales, selection and what it can establish
When a chart must be redrawn honest and colour-safe with its uncertainty shown
When you want a second pass or fail on axes, colours and chart type

tasks.task: Turn brand colours into an accessible chart palette

items.when: When charts should use brand colours and some may fail accessibility checks
When the palette must pass contrast, colour-blind, greyscale and dark mode checks
When the brand colours are only on the live site and must be measured first
When the brand has too few usable colours, to plan a small added palette with one job each
When each text and background pair needs testing, with the nearest passing colour

tasks.task: Write alt text and a long description for a chart

items.when: When a chart goes on a site, PDF, deck or email and needs text alternatives
When colour is the only cue and labels or patterns must carry the meaning too
When the charts sit in a deck, to check titles, reading order and alt text
When the charts sit on a web page that must work with keyboard and screen reader

tasks.task: Plan a one-page infographic

items.when: When numbers, steps or results need one main message and sections in reading order
Before layout, to plan which visual pairs with which words so the point sticks
When the client wants to see a finished version with a layout and style picked
When the page looks like a stock template, to get three hand-made alternatives
When the page carries a lot of text and needs a grid and a short type list
When decoration crowds the numbers, to keep only what helps people compare
When the layout is drafted, to see where the eye lands first and what to cut

tasks.task: Plan a data carousel or infographic set for social posts

items.when: When results must become slides for Instagram or LinkedIn, one fact per slide
When the set is for LinkedIn, to try a different carousel script and opening slide
When a figure means little alone, to turn it into a comparison people can picture
When the client's team will build and reuse the slides themselves
Before posting, to check each figure on a slide against its source

tasks.task: Outline a results deck from a table

items.when: When there is a spreadsheet of results and a meeting, with one message per slide
When the data is messy and must be cleaned and checked before the story is built
When you want a second storyboard built as a deck to compare
When the client needs a PowerPoint file with real editable text, tables and charts
When the deck is a pile of charts, to shape it into a story with a clear ask
Before the deck is sent, to check every slide number and chart against the workbook

tasks.task: Refresh the charts for a recurring report

items.when: Monthly or quarterly, when new figures land for a report, board pack or results page
When a deck needs every number updated from new figures, with a change log
When the monthly workbook and its update deck are built together
When the new deck should be compared with last month's for every changed number
When each chart and label must agree with the source workbook

tasks.task: Write a chart style guide for the client's reports

items.when: When the guide needs a tested palette, text sizes and labelling rules
When colour, type and grid need firm rules every chart and page must follow
When the client has no report fonts, to compare three pairs with sizes
When developers will apply the guide and need tokens and a handoff spec
Before the guide is issued, to test every colour pair in light and dark

tasks.task: Write chart code for an app or website

items.when: When the site needs a runnable Chart.js config or Vega-Lite spec for each chart
When hover, zoom and pan matter, to try an embeddable interactive version
When several charts with filters should ship as one page that works offline
When the charts are live on a page, to test them against accessibility rules

tasks.task: Build or fix charts in Excel and PowerPoint

items.when: When the client builds charts in a spreadsheet and needs the type and steps
When a deck holds picture charts that must become editable ones from real data
When charts and text must follow the client's own slide template
When the charts are placed, to prove each value matches the workbook

tasks.task: Lay out a one-page results summary

items.when: When a year or project must fit one page with a big number, a chart and three facts
When the source is a long report, to get the answer and the numbers that matter first
When the page looks like every other summary, to get three alternatives
When the page is drafted, to check type size, spacing and line length

tasks.task: Design a dashboard page readers take in at a glance

items.when: When you know who reads it and what they decide, to pick metrics and a layout
When the tool is Power BI and pages, charts and filters need laying out
When a working sample with sliders or toggles would settle the layout
When there is a mockup, for feedback on hierarchy and consistency with fixes

tasks.task: Make charts for an annual or impact report

items.when: When a report needs a consistent set of charts taken from brief to print
When key figures should also be shown as comparisons readers can picture
When captions state claims, to find each one that needs a source
When the client is a charity, to check facts, numbers and names before print

tasks.task: Chart survey results fairly

items.when: When survey results need a findings table, caveats and a slide-by-slide briefing
When each survey question needs the right chart with its base size shown
When small groups are compared, to show what the numbers cannot tell you
Before charting, to see which answers can be trusted and which are weak

tasks.task: Draw a process diagram or flowchart

items.when: Before drawing, to plan a diagram that pairs with the explanation
When the diagram should be text the client can paste into docs and edit
When a finished picture is wanted, to get a clean SVG version
When the diagram shows a workflow, to check each hand-off as it is drawn

tasks.task: Design a map of the numbers

items.when: When figures vary by place and need a map with symbols, labels and readability checks
When shaded areas may mislead because big regions hold few people

tasks.task: Make figures for a paper or a research poster

items.when: When results or a method need charts and diagrams fit for a paper
When figures must be colour-safe, show uncertainty and export at journal size
When approved text and figures must become an editable poster at print size
Before submission, to check each figure for chart type, axes and colour problems

tasks.task: Plan icons and pictures for an infographic

items.when: When the page needs a small icon set and a test that each icon reads
When one picture is needed, with a prompt, the exact size and a file plan
When a long piece needs a plan for where pictures belong and a matching set
When the pictures are placed, to have a fresh reviewer read the page as the client would

tasks.task: Animate a chart or infographic for social or video

items.when: When a static design should move, with fidelity checks and video or GIF exports
When an editor will build it and needs an exact plan and a sourced text table
When the animation is drafted, to check the chart still reads true at each stage

tasks.task: Get a results deck ready to present and share

items.when: When the deck is finished and needs notes, appendix links and an accessibility pass
When the presenter needs notes with sources, transitions and a rehearsal plan
Before sharing, to fix slide titles, reading order and alt text

always.when: Before delivery, to have a fresh reviewer read the work against the brief as the client would
Before anything is published, to catch typos and a measure named two ways
When a headline or caption states a figure you cannot trace to the client's data

helpers.when: When the numbers are messy or the finding is not yet worked out
When the charts must live in a dashboard with defined metrics and a refresh
When the infographic needs full artwork, print files or a social template kit
When the deck needs slide design and a template beyond the charts
When a report or page must pass a formal accessibility audit
When charts must be built into a live site or app with real data

gaps: No library item writes a Vega-Lite spec or a Chart.js config; the chart makers produce Python, Plotly or MATLAB output
No library item gives step-by-step chart building in Excel or Google Sheets
No library item scores a chart for cut axes, dual axes, crowded pies or misleading colour; only one imported agent checks charts
No library item tests a chart palette for colour-blind readers and greyscale; the contrast checker is for interface colours
No library item writes alt text or a long description for a chart; the alt text items are for product photos
No library item plans a data carousel for Instagram or LinkedIn; the carousel writers are for ads
No library item renders three clearly different chart or infographic directions as images to compare
No library item writes a chart style guide: palette, type, labels, number formats and when to use each chart
No library item writes the headline and annotations that say what a chart shows
No library item decides when a table beats a chart, or designs a readable table
